artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan unifying the Stage MT-4 lock-touching session-id sites onto the bare $session_id, adding a register/acquire parity regression group to test-conflict-predicate.sh, stating the parity invariant in task-lock.md, and gating on full verification plus a follow-up record for the identical pattern in the three multi-task command files.

memory_candidates.content: Self-exclusion predicates keyed on an exact identifier string make any per-consumer decoration of that identifier a self-contention bug. In the task-lock session registry, a batch registers once under a bare session_id (with a UNION file_scope over all batch members), but each per-task acquire passed a task-suffixed ${session_id}_${task_num}. session_contention()'s D4 exclusion 1 is `select($sess.session_id != $own_sid)` -- an exact match -- so the batch's own registration was never excluded and every acquire refused against the batch's own union scope. The failure is deterministic and total, not a race. Generalizable rule: whenever a component registers under an identifier and a later stage re-presents that identifier to a predicate that self-excludes by equality, the two construction sites form a parity invariant that must be stated at the point of use, not left implicit. Related consumers that decorate the same id for provenance (commit --session, defect-record --session, status-sync) are safe precisely because nothing self-excludes on them -- so the audit question is not 'is the id consistent everywhere' but 'which consumers compare it for identity'. The same register-bare/acquire-suffixed shape exists in commands/research.md, commands/plan.md, and commands/implement.md.
